label: At D2, high after a1 reaches S2 (rare), low after a2 reaches S1; S2 after no reward raises it.
terms: (phase == D2) * (action == 1) * (state == 2) ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 2) * (state == 1) ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 1) * (state == 1) ;; (phase == D2) * (state == 2) * (prev_reward == 0) ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 2) * (state == 2) * belief_lo ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 1) * (state == 1) * belief_lo ;; (phase != D2) * belief_lo ;; (phase != D2) * (prev_action == 1) * (prev_reward == 0)
explanation: Raw candidate n of unit 25 sits near -1 at D1/GO and rises at D2; its magnitude beyond timing is almost entirely set at D2 by the just-made choice x reached state (both observed at D2): a1->S2 (rare) drives it strongly up (~+0.86), a2->S1 (rare) pushes it down (~-0.4), and reaching S2 after an unrewarded previous trial adds ~+0.2. So it is an S2-reached / rare-a1 detector modulated by previous loss. The free fit adds a smaller a1->S1 decrement, belief log-odds slopes within common transitions at D2 (higher when belief favors S1, i.e. S2 surprising), and small D1/GO effects (belief_lo, after a1 unrewarded), raising dev R2 from 0.76 to 0.84. No future variables used.

issues: I reproduced the short form's test R^2 beyond timing at 0.747 (weights +0.855 / -0.397 / +0.215). That is about 89% of the observed-only additive ceiling (0.84) and 90% of the free fit (0.83).

Every term is needed. Dropping the S2-after-loss term gives 0.696. Swapping it for D2*belief_lo gives 0.696, D2*S2*belief_lo 0.717, D2*S2*belief 0.741, D2*prev_reward==0 without the state 0.715, D2*S1*prev_reward==0 0.698, and D2*a1*prev_reward==0 0.697. So the specific claim 'S2 after no reward' holds up. Writing it as S2*(1-prev_reward) or (state!=1)*(prev_reward==0) scores the same (0.747).
The profile supports the choice x state claims. The D2 residual is a1S2 +0.90, a2S1 -0.43, a1S1 -0.13 and a2S2 about 0.
Minor omission: a1->S1 (common) at D2 is also somewhat low (-0.13). Adding it instead of the reward term gives only 0.726, and the label does not mention it.
Misses show modest systematic errors, none large. At D1/GO the prediction is about 0.03 too low, worst after a1 S2 u (+0.10 to +0.12). At D2 it is too high after a1 S2 r (-0.156) and a2 S2 r (-0.11).

The worst single windows are common a2->S2 at D2 during long unrewarded streaks: actual about +0.5 to +0.7, predicted about -0.2. The S2-after-loss term captures the direction of this but underestimates its size when losses repeat. That leaves some unexplained graded variance, which looks like accumulated losses or belief.
